reports.title: Bull Shoals Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing is fair. Best suggestion is to get up early and look for surface activity. Topwater has been hit or miss. Try a small popper-style bait or Zara Spoon-style bait in natural colors. Del says he’s a fan of the Lucky Craft Gunfish. Fish around ledges, points, bluffs and swings. The Plopper and buzzbait bite should pick up once the lake generation slows. Those sunfish will pull up. Fish are still in the summer areas. Largemouth bass are really grouped up. Powerfishing shallow in the creeks is still hit or miss. The baitfish are pulling back. The ol’ Big Red Worm, Texas-rigged, around trees and laydowns and 15-25 feet on points is working. reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text: The University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff Bass Fishing Team reports water temperatures in the upper 80s. Black bass have slid out to the outer edges and points of jetties, especially if wind is pushing on or across those points. Expect to find freshwater drum, white bass, striped bass, catfish and both spotted and largemouth bass hanging out on the same productive jetty points; so, if you get a bite on a jetty, keep casting to the same spot and nearby a few more times at least, as that fish likely was not alone.

“Conveniently, for those shallow water fisherman, many quality largemouth and spotted bass have been shallow.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text:
Bass, especially largemouth, have been scattered but catchable. Bass are like humans when it’s hot: They seek shade, cooler temps and an easily accessible food supply. The drop-shot rig with a watermelon seed Zoom Trick Worm rigged wacky, or nose-hooked shad-collared fluke, produces the best numbers of bass (especially spotted bass ).
Crappie are fair at best under docks. Shooting a small fluke on a jighead up into and under structure can catch crappie, but don’t expect large numbers. Docks near current are best, as these predators exclusively eat baitfish. “Good Luck and Go Greeson!”

reports.text: (updated 8-12-2021) Del Colvin at Bull Shoals Lake Boat Dock said that for bass fishing, anglers should continue to beat the heat and get up early, and they should plan to use topwater baits like poppers and Zara Spooks in the creeks.

reports.title: Arkansas River (Little Rock Area Pools) fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been a little tough, they report. Anglers are doing OK on black/blue green pumpkin jigs on the main river around jetties or sand drops, and on topwater baits and buzzbaits around grass in the mornings. Bass are also being caught on square-bill crankbaits in 5-6 feet depth. Catfish are good below Murray Lock and Dam on cut bait, stink bait and nightcrawlers. (updated 7-29-2021) Zimmerman’s Exxon (501-944-2527) said Thursday morning that crappie are good around brush and laydowns on the river, 10-12 feet deep, and biting on Bobby Garland Baby Shad in glitter critter color. Bream are good on crickets in the backwaters in 3-4 feet of water. Catfish are good below the dams on…

reports.title: Brewer Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie reports are good; anglers are trolling deeper in 6-7 feet of water down the middle of the lake for best results. Also, make sure to use size 6 crappie minnows; that’s what they’re favoring. Black bass are good, with best results coming in the evenings in the weeds. Bass minnows, buzzbaits and Rooster Tails will work best.

“Wow,” he says about that temp. “ Crappie fishing is changing with water levels and water temperatures.

Darryl Morris of Family Fishing Trips (501-844-5418) says white bass and black bass…

reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text: Largemouth bass bite is fair. The Kentucky bass (spotted bass) bite is also fair, with some reports of them being found in 15-20 feet off drops and rocky banks. The better bass bite of this week helped on Tuesday njight as Noah White and Greg White caught 12.94 pounds of bass, edging Cameron Nesterenko and Andrew Wooley’s 12.43 pounds; Nesterenko and Wooley found the 4.74 Big Bass, though.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Overcup fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie also are fair but slowing. Black bass are good, with nice-size bass being caught lately. Shad, large shiners and bass minnows will all attract the catfish bite.
Bass are doing well around the brushtops on plastic worms and frogs. Crappie are slow but anglers are still catching some good ones in 12-14 feet of water 3-5 feet down.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Arkansas River fishing report
reports.text:
Black bass are doing pretty well on small white and black buzzbaits in shallow water on the main river and in the backwaters. Also, a quarter-ounce shaky head worm in 16 feet of water on the main river has been working, and shad-colored crankbaits fished around the jetties on the main river have gotten bass.
Black bass are being caught in the early mornings off the end of rock jetties using black/red tubes and Firetiger Bomber Crankbaits. Crappie are said to be fair.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie are in the brush and also suspended anywhere from 12-20 feet deep. Bass are good early and late. Look in river arms for some better quality largemouth. “Heard of some nice bass being caught on large plastic worms up in the White River.
Crappie are good. Some crappie are in the cover and some are being caught in open water. Black bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Tailwater fishing report
reports.text: Kentucky bass are being caught between Beaver town and Holiday Island throwing soft plastics at chunk rock and structure.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Bishop Park Ponds fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been fair with minnows, floating worms and small topwater baits. Crappie have been slow but some small ones have been biting #4 and pink minnows.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Crown Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie reports are fair. Black bass are good early in the mornings and late evenings. Like crappie, they’re running deep now, at about 25 feet depth.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: DeGray Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are slow in brushpiles; fish the ones that are just out of the thermocline and fish near the bottom. Brushpiles are full of fish – it’s just that they are full of little bream and bass about 3-inches long, too. Black bass are in their summer pattern.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Greers Ferry Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Crappie action is still great spider-rigging and vertical-fishing with minnows, small crankbaits and jigs fished 15-30 feet deep. Black bass are schooling, some are shallow chasing bream, and some are sitting and staying on structure out to 45 feet deep. A gauntlet of baits are working on the bass.
Black bass are biting well in the early mornings and late evenings on Carolina rigs, deep-diving crankbaits and big swimbaits in 20 feet of water.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Harris Brake Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are good. Black bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Beaverfork fishing report
reports.text: Angler Dennis Charles reports that there has been no change in the fishing from last week to this one, other than bass are hiding in the grass. The bass bite has been good; anglers are finding success using spinnerbaits, plastic worms, topwaters, chatterbaits, buzzbaits, frogs and jigs. Crappie are fair, use jigs in black/chartreuse, or minnows. Bass are good.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Charles fishing report
reports.text: “Lots of fishing going on,” she said, though the only actual report she received was on bass and bream. Black bass were good, with spinnerbaits, crankbaits, dark plastic worms, topwater lures and regular worms working. The best bass fishing was around brush or rocket points focusing at 4.5-5.5 feet depth. No reports on crappie or catfish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Maumelle fishing report
reports.text: L argemouth bass bite is fair. The Kentucky bass (spotted bass) bite is also fair, with some reports of them being found in 15-20 feet off drops and rocky banks. No one broke double-digits in pounds in Tuesday night’s black bass tournament; Matt Hedrick and Kevin Hannah won with a five-bass stringer of 9.04 pounds edging Robert and Tracy White’s 8.87 pounds. Gary Harris and Rudy Westbrook did land a nice bass for Big Bass, a 5.48-pounder.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Nimrod fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent. In a crappie tournament there last week, Brandon Smith caught seven crappie weighing a total of 14 pounds. Anglers are finding the crappie 3 feet deep in 6-8 feet of water. Black bass are good; they’re in 8-10 feet depth.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report

reports.text: Bass fishing has been good early in the morning and at night. Crappie have been biting well for a few anglers using No.

reports.text: Todd Gadberry at Mountain Harbor Resort and Spa (870-867-2191/800-832-2276 out of state) reports that black bass are still slow to fair. Crappie are slow.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Sequoyah fishing report
reports.text: Crappie are excellent. Black bass are fair; go with topwater baits.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Winona fishing report
reports.text: Bass fishing has been fair with Carolina-rigged plastics, chatterbaits, buzzbaits and live minnows. Crappie are biting slow and are scattered out, but some good ones have been hitting No.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text:
Mike Siefert at Millwood Lake Guide Service noted that Millwood Lake has received 611,275 Florida-strain black bass fingerlings stocked this year from the AGFC, and also the AGFC has added another 40-50 PVC fishing attractors in Saratoga, Beard’s Bluff, Cottonshed and Okay Landing areas.
* Largemouth bass: They’ve been in their typical summer habits and haunts for last few weeks. Juvenile largemouths are breaking on threadfin shad early in multiple locations, near and in lily pads for short duration periods. Bass Assassin Shads, Johnson Chrome Spoons with a short grub trailer, or H&H Short-Arm Spinnerbaits will work through the pads when bass move into the pads to feed for quick cycles…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Saline River Access in Benton fishing report
reports.text: Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said bass are in the current and just below the shoals. Crappie have been biting in some deep backwaters and along sunken logs that are in or near current. 4 crappie minnow on small hooks and light, clear line fished under a small bobber is the best rig to use.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text: For the smallmouth bass, olive skull heads are great and olive Woolies with lead eyes, tied Clouser-style, and of course crawfish patterns. “The smallmouth really like a fast-dropping fly and hit a lot of times on the drop.”

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Sunset Lake fishing report
reports.text: Crappie have been biting fair for some. 6 minnows and pink crappie minnows or Bobby Garland Baby Shad Jigs have been working. Bass have been more active early and late in the day and are hitting Carolina-rigged and floating plastics as well as topwater baits and buzzbaits.

reports.title: Arkansas River at Morrilton fishing report
reports.text: Charlie Hoke at Charlie’s Hidden Harbor at Oppelo (501-354-8080) said the black bass are mainly being caught in the early morning on topwater baits, and jitterbugs “seem like doing pretty good,” he said, as well as spinnerbaits going across the water. The bass bite is fair, not great, he said. No report on crappie.

reports.text: “The Kentucky bass have been a little more active this week as well. The bass responded well to hard crankbaits and suspended soft plastics, thrown at structure.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Lake Hamilton fishing report
reports.text: Bass have already started to blend into their fall patterns. The shad binge is beginning to appear and the bass are HEAVY with full bellies. Largemouth are starting to move into shallow areas in creek channels and near or in grass, brush or docks. Spotted bass can still be found offshore in water depths up to 25 feet and actively hunting large baitfish balls in open water or over chunk rock and brush. These scavengers love cheese and hot dogs! “ Crappie are fixing to really pop off when the water temps drop a little more!

reports.text: Westrock Landing (501-658-5598) on Highway 10 near Roland says largemouth bass are slow. Some reports coming in this week say the black bass can be found in 8-12 feet and 16-20 feet. (Anglers, please note that the Fall/Winter Bass League season will start Oct. Kentucky bass are fair. Some can still be found mixed in with the crappie on the flats or near brushpiles in 8-12 feet. Crappie are fair.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouths continue in their typical, full-blown summer patterns, Mike says, with not a lot of changes over the past week. Once the sun climbs and begins surface penetration, the surface temp will climb several degrees and the bass continue retreating to the first and second drops out of the flats and deeper sections of the creeks or the river behind primary and secondary points out of river current. The topwater bite over the past few weeks seems to be best for overall surface activity just after daylight, especially cloud cover days, and “it appears to us the largemouth bass are night feeding. Some mornings when we arrive at dawn, we can hear bass breaking shallow before we ever get to…

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Spring River fishing report
reports.text: Best technique for smallmouth is a cast at an angle downstream and a short fast strip back. Pumkin Crappie Magnets are perfect for smallmouth, too. And I will tell ya right now, a smallmouth bass on a trout Slayer Rod is a complete blast!”

reports.text:
Lisa Spencer at Lisa’s Bait Shop (501-778-6944) said crappie have been slow but are biting No. 6 crappie minnows. Bass been good on topwater baits, plastic lizards and brooder minnows.
As for hot spots in the vicinity, Lisa says that for two weeks in a row she’s been hearing a lot of people are catching lots of little bass and then some nice-size crappie at Lake Nimrod. 12 bass minnows there. Bass species are doing well not only deep, but shallow. Behind, beside or under docks and slips can pay good dividends when seeking bass. If it’s the middle of the day and high noon (if you can stand it), go deeper off islands and points where bass and hybrids are suspending together and attacking large baitfish balls.

I switched methods of fishing and started casting a deep-diving crankbait over the tops of some brush where I was marking fish and landed a nice 12 crappie and a few bass.

reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Largemouths continue in their typical, full-blown summer patterns. Once the the sun climbs and begins intense surface penetration, the surface temp will climb several degrees, and the bass are retreating to the first and second drops out of the flats and deeper sections of the creeks or the river behind primary and secondary points out of river current. “We have been finding decent largemouth bass hitting jigging spoons in Little River behind primary points from 7-10 a.m., and the bite shuts off. reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Norfork Lake fishing report
reports.text: I caught and released walleye, bass, bluegills, crappie and catfish. I believe I boated over 20 fish, but only the spotted bass and a few crappie were keeper size. I marked some nice-size bass suspended 10-15 feet down near bluff line points. I found crappie just stacked at the top of the brush. I still only had the 1-ounce spoon tied on, but the crappie were aggressive. Several of the crappie were 10-11 inches, but most were on the short side.”

reports.title: Lake Fort Smith fishing report
reports.text: The bass are on the move and are working on schools of shad, and if you time it just right you can catch some lunker. But you’ve got to hit it just as the bass coral the shad up in the shallows in the evening just before dark. Look for bass in 4-6 feet depth. No reports on crappie or catfish.

reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Beaver Lake fishing report
reports.text: Bass are fair at night – try black spinnerbaits and buzzbaits. Some bass are schooling early. Crappie are being caught pushing or pulling cranks and jigs. Walleye are fair on crawler harnesses “and another method I use is trolling spinnerbaits on braided line through flooded timber for suspended walleye. Spinnerbaits will deflect most of the time off branches without hang ups. Graph the fish they are sometimes in the tops or other times more in middle of the timber. White works well.” Catfishing is good up the War Eagle arm at night on liver. “Hang in there. Fall is not far off. Still, if you work at it you can catch them,” Jon says. reports.source: Arkansas Game and Fish weekly fishing report
reports.title: Millwood Lake fishing report
reports.text: Mike says crappie have been on FIRE and consistently biting minnows for the past few weeks in the standing timber of the oxbows and planted brush piles along Little River, just out of river current behind primary or secondary points. Minnows have been seeing the best bite over the past few weeks with an occasional largemouth or white bass stealing it. Good slabs up to 2.5 pounds are biting well, best from daylight to around 10-11 a.m. when the bite almost shuts off like the largemouths. Most of the crappie have been holding from 4-9 feet of depth around cypress trees where deeper drops are nearby.
